newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers mixed in quiet holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers mixed in quiet holiday trade.

text.p: North American bunker prices were mixed and mostly quiet early this week, with action in Houston to the upside the one notable exception to the subdued pre-holiday trade, traders said.

"It's quiet right now, but I think it'll pick up on Thursday and Friday," said one East and Gulf Coast trader. The New Year's Day holiday closed the NYMEX early on Tuesday, and will keep it closed until Thursday.
In Houston, both 380 CST and 180 CST climbed $5 on Monday to between $114/115 a tonne and $118/119 a tonne respectively.
Prices in New York were stable across the board.
But prices in Norfolk, while pulling back a touch from recent highs, were still considerably higher than in New York, with traders suspecting some sort of logistical difficulty behind the strength.
New York 380 and 180 CST prices were at about $117/120 and $123/126 a tonne respectively, while in Norfolk those same fuels were at $131/132 and $135/136 a tonne respectively.

Prices on the West Coast meanwhile lost a bit of ground amid the thin talk in the last 10 days brought on by the holidays. Los Angeles 380 and 180 CST both lost about $2 and stood at about $118 and $124 a tonne respectively.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
